info.title: API.SH: WorkIndia
info.description: The WorkIndia API from API.SH: public WorkIndia data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
An employer's open jobs on WorkIndia (employers that have a WorkIndia company page, e.g. Zomato), optionally in one city, with the page title, description, the cities it hires in and the jobs (same fields as search). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/workindia-company

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Company name or its WorkIndia company page link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The filter values WorkIndia offers for a role and city: roles (industry), qualifications, experience, areas of the city, work types, gender, extra keywords, courses and related job titles, each with its value and page link, plus the page's FAQ.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/workindia-filters

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Pass value (comma separated for several) as the filter of the same name to /workindia/v1/search; job_title values work as q.

get.description:
One WorkIndia job in full: title, company, role, city, area, address, interview address, salary text and monthly range, experience, qualification, gender, English level, timings, interview details, openings, requirements, the full description (text and HTML), posting and expiry dates, views, breadcrumbs and the employer's HR contact (`contact_type`, `contact`, usually a phone number, and `contact_person`). Pass an id or the job link; `latest=true` returns the newest job.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/workindia-job

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (the number at the end of the job link).

parameters.name: latest
parameters.description: true: the newest job on the site.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Searches WorkIndia's jobs (delivery, drivers, back office, sales, telecalling, helpers and other everyday jobs across India) by role words and city, with the site's filters: industry (role), qualification, experience, area, work type, gender, course and extra keywords, sorted newest first, by relevance or by score. Role words are matched to WorkIndia's roles the way its own search pages do ("data entry" in Delhi becomes the back office role); the matched filters come back in `applied_filters`. 20 jobs per page, each with `id`, `title`, `url`, company, role, city, area, zone, state, pincode, address, monthly salary text and range, employment type, experience, qualification, gender, English level, timings, interview details, openings, posting and expiry dates, views and the description. Each job also carries the employer's HR contact (`contact_type`, `contact`, usually a phone number, and `contact_person`). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/workindia-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Role words, e.g. delivery boy, accountant, data entry, driver.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City, e.g. mumbai, pune, delhi, bangalore.

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Role value(s) from /workindia/v1/filters, e.g. delivery, back_office (comma separated).

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Area name(s) inside the city, e.g. Thane West (comma separated).

parameters.name: work_type
parameters.description: Work type value(s), e.g. work_from_home, part_time, night_shift (comma separated).

parameters.name: course
parameters.description: Course value(s), e.g. btech, bcom (comma separated).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
